Subject:  Proposed Schedule of Fees Fiscal Year 2024-25

RECOMMENDED ACTION: Provide a recommendation to the City Council concerning
adoption of the Fiscal Year 2024-25 Schedule of Fees.

FISCAL IMPACT: The Schedule of Fees establishes the amount the City can charge for
fees for service. The City’s annual budget typically includes approximately $5.0 million in
revenue from Service Charges and approximately $4.0 million in revenue from Licenses
and Permits.

DISCUSSION: A fee study is currently underway as referenced later in this staff report.
The current fee schedule proposal allows for a schedule to be in place until the fee study
and an updated schedule is ready for Council adoption and subsequent implementation.
It is anticipated that a new fee schedule will be provided to Council for consideration and
possible adoption early in FY 2024-25.

State law mandates that agencies such as the City of Malibu charge customers only the
fees necessary to recover costs for the services provided and prohibits charging fees
beyond the services rendered. If the FY 2024-25 fee schedule is approved, the revised
fees will not generate funds that exceed this standard.

In FY 2015-16, the City completed a comprehensive fee study that analyzed all fees and
charges for services. The rates established in the fee study have been used as a base
amount that have been increased annually with a cost-of-living adjustment.

Due to the annual increase based on inflation only, and changes in operations and staffing
since FY 2015-16, the City was overdue for conducting a study to ensure fees are in
alignment with full cost recovery; such studies typically result in some fees being updated,

 removed, or new ones added. To initiate a review of the City’s existing fee structure, a
Request for Proposals (RFP) was issued on August 3, 2023, and closed on August 29,
2023. The City chose and entered into an agreement with Matrix Consulting Group, Ltd.
(Matrix) in November 2023, with initiation in January 2024.

The project is underway, and Matrix is conducting a comprehensive study that will include,
data collection, interviews, production of a cost allocation plan (for internal and indirect
costs), an updated Schedule of Fees, presentation of results, and a new fee workbook for
updating annually. Their work is anticipated to be completed in April 2024. A revised fee
schedule will be provided to Council for consideration early in FY 2024-25, and if adopted,
will replace this proposed fee schedule.

Pending completion of the study, staff have applied a cost-of-living adjustment to the
established Schedule of Fees and currently propose no additional changes for FY 2024-
25. The cost-of-living adjustment is derived from the Consumer Price Index (CPI) using an
annual percentage from February. The percentage change of CPI was 4.3% in February
2024, and this adjustment has been included in the interim Schedule of Fees for FY 2024-
25.

The proposed Schedule of Fees for FY 2024-25 is attached for review and will be
presented to Council on April 22, 2024.

MINUTES
  MALIBU ADMINISTRATION & FINANCE SUBCOMMITTEE
  SPECIAL MEETING
  APRIL 10, 2024
  CITY HALL SURFRIDER ROOM
  2:00 P.M.

CALL TO ORDER

  Mayor Pro Tem Stewart called the meeting to order at 2:01 p.m.

ROLL CALL

  The following persons were recorded in attendance:

  PRESENT: Mayor Pro Tem Doug Stewart and Councilmember Bruce Silverstein

  ALSO PRESENT: Steve McClary, City Manager; Joseph Toney, Assistant City Manager;
  Rene’e Neerrnann, Finance Manager; Adrian Fernandez, Assistant Planning Director; and
  Cynthia Alba, Executive Assistant.

REPORT ON POSTING OF AGENDA

  Executive Assistant Alba reported that the agenda for the meeting was properly posted on
  posted on April 3, 2024.

APPROVAL OF AGENDA

MOTION  Councilmember Silverstein moved, and Mayor Pro Tem Stewart seconded a motion
  to approve the agenda. The question was called, and the motion carried
  unanimously.

ITEM 1  PRESENTATIONS

  None.

ITEM 2  OLD BUSINESS

  None.

ITEM 3  NEW BUSINESS

  A.  Proposed Schedule of Fees for Fiscal Year 2024-25
  Recommended Action: Provide a recommendation to the City Council concerning
  adoption of the Fiscal Year 2024-25 Schedule of Fees.
 Malibu Administration and Finance Subcommittee
Special Meeting
Minutes of April 10, 2024
Page 2 of 5

  Assistant City Manager Toney reviewed the staff report and noted that there was a
  typo on page two of the staff report, the CPI should state 3.4 percent and not 4.3
  percent. He explained that the fee schedule numbers would be placeholders until
  the fee schedule study is concluded sometime around the end of the fiscal year. He
  explained that the fee schedule adopted at that time would change the rates for the
  fees. However, in the meantime, they are presenting numbers to account for
  inflation, which would be 3.4 percent under February’s CPI.

  Councilmember Silverstein stated that he would like more information regarding
  the laws surrounding fees.

  City Manager McClary stated that some of those could fall under Prop 218 and
  added that they could work on getting the specific code section.

  Assistant City Manager Toney stated that fees are specific and also include time
  spent on the project.

  Councilmember Silverstein inquired for more information regarding the differences
  in fees for complex projects and simpler proj ects.

  Assistant Manager Toney used a water heater as a sample, where fees would be
  nominal due to needed staff time. He explained that the initial fee would be the
  same with fluctuating staff time. However, if projects were to change it would
  entail other fees.

  Mayor Pro Tem Stewart reviewed page one of the schedule and pointed out the
  different levels of tiers for complex items.

  Finance Manager Neermann said that some of the fees are already designed with
  tiers to allow for complexity. For example, the Building Plan Check is at an hourly
  rate, with a one—hour minimum.

  City Manager McClary stated that he asked Assistant Flaming Director Adrian
  Fernandez to join the discussion to help clarify the fees for their department.

  Mayor Pro Tem pointed out page five as an example of the hourly plan check costs.

  City Manager McClary added that there is a limit to the number of resubmissions
  before they become eligible for more fees.

  Assistant City Manager Toney reviewed the details ofthe fee study currently taking
  place, where average times taken to work on an item are taken into consideration.
  He stated that the last time a fee study was conducted was in 2015.

  Councilmember Silverstein inquired how often fee studies are required to be
  updated.
 Malibu Administration and Finance Subcommittee
Special Meeting
Minutes ofApril 10, 2024
Page 3 of 5

  Assistant City Manager Toney explained that they should be conducted Within a
  reasonable time. He stated that cities could easily fall behind on updates, and if a
  fee schedule is not updated within a reasonable time, they could see increases, such
  as a five-dollar fee going up to 35 dollars.

  Mayor Pro Tem explained that fees are very granular and that there is an art to the
  fee schedule. He said that the fees must be reasonable and to scale.

  Assistant City Manager Toney stated that the fee study aims to capture those
  comments regarding scale.

  Councilmember Silverstein inquired regarding setting fees for facility use.

  Assistant City Manager Toney stated that the city cannot make proflts off services
  and stated that he would gather more information.

  Assistant Planning Director Fernandez responded to an earlier inquiry regarding
  fees and their varying levels of complexity by using administrative plan review and
  the 6 levels that correlate with the item. He explained that having different levels
  leads to fair fees. He added that in the past, they tried doing this part in an hourly
  pay model, and it led to more staff time needing to track and submit time invoices
  for different proj ects that can be disputable. He added that new commercial proj ects
  do require a $20,000 deposit. He added that projects, although the same in nature
  can take more time than others based on different factors such as appeals.

  Mayor Pro Tem inquired regarding the varying price tiers.

  Assistant City Manager Toney stated that the department is looking at improving
  the processes by looking at the possibility of rapid permits. He stated that the City
  of Oakland is a great example.

  Mayor Pro Tem Stewart emphasized the importance of having greater numbers of
  compliance if permits are more accessible.

  Assistant Flaming Director Fernandez stated for over~the—counter applications, a
  one-hour fee is collected. He added that all fixtures do require a permit. He added
  that the fees cover processing of the permit and inspections for the most part.

  Mayor Pro Tem Stewart added that this is an opportunity to keep things simple to
  encourage compliance. He confirmed that the increase was 3.4 percent across the
  board according to February’s CPI and inquired if there were any items that were
  over or undercharged.
 Malibu Administration and Finance Subcommittee
Special Meeting
Minutes of April 10, 2024
Page 4 of 5

  Assistant City Manager Toney stated that the information is unknown and still
  being researched as part of the fee study. He added that it's not necessarily 3.4
  percent across the board, and some fees will not change.

  Assistant Flaming Director Fernandez explained that there may be expected room
  for increases in planning fees as the fees have been heavily subsidized in the past
  and have not been changed in past years.

  Assistant City Manager Toney stated that this would need to be a Council policy
  discussion on Whether they wish to keep using general taxpayer funds on elected
  services that other residents elect to do.

  Councilmember Silverstein inquired if they could make a motion to keep the fees
  the same until they receive the fee study results.

  Mayor Pro Tem Stewart reiterated that he is most worried about compliance and
  risk management and is also willing to wait for the fee study results.

  Councilmember Silverstein inquired about code enforcement Violation fees.

  Assistant Flaming Director Fernandez added that there are penalties for municipal
  code violations.

  Mayor Pro Tem Stewart explained that there is a fee for towing cars and fines for
  parking in the wrong space, he added that it is a fine as opposed to a fee.

  Finance Manager Neermann reviewed article 13.b. in the California Constitution
  and Props 218, 413, and 26.

MOTION  Mayor Pro Tem Stewart moved, and Councilmember Silverstein seconded a motion
  to recommend to the City Council to keep fees unchanged until the fee study results
  have been completed, research self-certification or simple compliance. The
  question was called, and the motion carried unanimously.
